The zoning ordinances adopted by Hardin, with proper enforcement, futher insure orderly development.
The Crow Tribe has also taken the opportunity to adopt various codes and ordinances in order that development may be regulated. On Janary 31, 1976 an Environmental Health and Sanitation Ordinance, Land-Use Zoning Ordinance, Crow Law and Order Code, and an Ordinance creating a method for taxation of coal were adopted. Should the above-named codes and ordinances be approved their effectiveness will lie upon the enforcement and regulatory procedures implemented by the Crow Tribal Council.
One strong indicator of Tribal interest in planning will be the extent of Crow participation in the 208 program for areawide water quality and waste treatment planning, and subsequent use by the Tribe of the funding and technical assistance available through the Mid-Yellow-stone Area Planning Organization according to P.L.92-500. No strong contacts now exist (Director, MYAPO, personal comm. February 12, 1976) although the planning staff is interested in reaching an agreement with the Crows concerning pollution sources assessment on Crow lands.
As previously indicated, a great deal more needs to be accomplished in developing planning institutions and the implementation of controls before it can be assumed that orderly development is highly probable.
There are numerous federal and state agencies which can provide various kinds of assistance in essentially all facets of the planning process. There are also numerous private consulting firms who will provide technical assistance to the local planning organizations.
